The test file added in this branch is `integration-tests/http/__tests__/customer/admin/customer.spec.ts` — an HTTP integration test.

Run it with:

```bash
yarn test:integration:http customer.spec.ts
```

(Jest matches on filename, so this runs just that spec.) If that doesn't scope correctly, use the path relative to the test root:

```bash
TEST_TYPE=integration:http yarn test:integration:http -- customer/admin/customer.spec.ts
```

The simplest and most reliable is usually just `yarn test:integration:http customer.spec.ts` — Jest's CLI treats trailing args as filename patterns.

```text
import { MedusaContainer } from "@medusajs/framework/types"
import {
  ContainerRegistrationKeys,
  remoteQueryObjectFromString,
} from "@medusajs/framework/utils"

export const refetchCustomer = async (
  customerId: string,
  scope: MedusaContainer,
  fields: string[]
) => {
  const remoteQuery = scope.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.REMOTE_QUERY)
  const queryObject = remoteQueryObjectFromString({
    entryPoint: "customer",
    variables: {
      filters: { id: customerId },
    },
    fields: fields,
  })

  const customers = await remoteQuery(queryObject)
  return customers[0]
}

export const getCustomerOrderStats = async (
  customerId: string,
  scope: MedusaContainer
) => {
  const remoteQuery = scope.resolve(ContainerRegistrationKeys.REMOTE_QUERY)
  const queryObject = remoteQueryObjectFromString({
    entryPoint: "customer",
    variables: {
      filters: { id: customerId },
    },
    fields: ["orders.id", "orders.total"],
  })

  const customers = await remoteQuery(queryObject)
  const orders: { total: number }[] = customers[0]?.orders ?? []

  return {
    order_count: orders.length,
    lifetime_value: orders.reduce((sum, order) => sum + (order.total ?? 0), 0),
  }
}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
          {

          },

        )

      await dbUtils.snapshot()
    })

          expect.objectContaining({

          expect.objectContaining({

        expect(response.data.customers).toEqual([

          expect.objectContaining({
            id: customer2.id,
          }),
          expect.objectContaining({

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.count).toEqual(1)
        expect(response.data.customers).toEqual(
          expect.arrayContaining([

            }),
          ])
        )
      })

            "/admin/customer-groups",

              name: "VIP 2",
            },
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.customer_group

        const group3 = (
          await api.post(
            "/admin/customer-groups",
            {
              name: "VIP 3",
            },
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.customer_group

        // Add with cg endpoint so we can test remove
        await api.post(
          `/admin/customer-groups/${group1.id}/customers`,
          {
            add: [customer1.id],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )

        const response = await api.post(
          `/admin/customers/${customer1.id}/customer-groups?fields=groups.id`,
          {
            remove: [group1.id],
            add: [group2.id, group3.id],
          },
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)

        expect(response.data.customer.groups.length).toEqual(2)
        expect(response.data.customer.groups).toEqual(
          expect.arrayContaining([
            expect.objectContaining({ id: group2.id }),
            expect.objectContaining({ id: group3.id }),
          ])
        )
      })
    })

    describe("GET /admin/customers/:id", () => {
      it("should fetch a customer", async () => {
        const response = await api.get(
          `/admin/customers/${customer1.id}`,
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.customer).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            id: customer1.id,
          })
        )
      })

      it("should fetch a customer with expand query", async () => {
        await api.post(
          `/admin/customers/${customer1.id}/addresses`,
          {
            first_name: "Lebron",
            last_name: "James",
            is_default_billing: true,
          },
          adminHeaders
        )

        // BREAKING: Customers no longer carry billing_address, they have addresses
        const response = await api.get(
          `/admin/customers/${customer1.id}?fields=*addresses,*groups`,
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.customer).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            id: customer1.id,
            addresses: [
              expect.objectContaining({
                is_default_billing: true,
                first_name: "Lebron",
                last_name: "James",
              }),
            ],
            groups: [],
          })
        )
      })

      it("should include order_count and lifetime_value based on the customer's orders", async () => {
        const customer = (
          await api.post(
            "/admin/customers",
            { email: "order-stats@email.com" },
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.customer

        const orderModule = container.resolve(Modules.ORDER)

        await orderModule.createOrders({
          customer_id: customer.id,
          currency_code: "usd",
          items: [{ title: "Test item 1", quantity: 1, unit_price: 5000 }],
        })

        await orderModule.createOrders({
          customer_id: customer.id,
          currency_code: "usd",
          items: [{ title: "Test item 2", quantity: 2, unit_price: 2500 }],
        })

        const response = await api.get(
          `/admin/customers/${customer.id}`,
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.customer.order_count).toEqual(2)
        // order totals: (1 * 5000) + (2 * 2500) = 10000, no tax/shipping applied
        expect(response.data.customer.lifetime_value).toEqual(10000)
      })

      it("should return zero order_count and lifetime_value for a customer with no orders", async () => {
        const customer = (
          await api.post(
            "/admin/customers",
            { email: "no-orders@email.com" },
            adminHeaders
          )
        ).data.customer

        const response = await api.get(
          `/admin/customers/${customer.id}`,
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data.customer.order_count).toEqual(0)
        expect(response.data.customer.lifetime_value).toEqual(0)
      })
    })

    describe("DELETE /admin/customers/:id", () => {
      it("should delete a customer and update auth identity", async () => {
        const registeredCustomerToken = (
          await api.post("/auth/customer/emailpass/register", {
            email: "test@email.com",
            password: "password",
          })
        ).data.token

        const customer = (
          await api.post(
            "/store/customers",
            {
              email: "test@email.com",
            },
            {
              headers: {
                Authorization: `Bearer ${registeredCustomerToken}`,
                ...storeHeaders.headers,
              },
            }
          )
        ).data.customer

        const response = await api.delete(
          `/admin/customers/${customer.id}`,
          adminHeaders
        )

        expect(response.status).toEqual(200)
        expect(response.data).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            id: customer.id,
            deleted: true,
            object: "customer",
          })
        )

        const { auth_identity_id } = jwt.decode(registeredCustomerToken)

        const authModule: IAuthModuleService = container.resolve(Modules.AUTH)

        const authIdentity = await authModule.retrieveAuthIdentity(
          auth_identity_id
        )

        expect(authIdentity).toEqual(
          expect.objectContaining({
            id: authIdentity.id,
            app_metadata: expect.not.objectContaining({
              customer_id: expect.any(String),
            }),
          })
        )
      })
    })
  },
})
```

Confirmed the reviewer is right — `getCustomerOrderStats` (packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/helpers.ts:25-42) only queries `orders.total`, never `orders.currency_code`, and just does a flat `reduce` sum. If a customer has a USD order and a EUR order, they get silently added together into a meaningless number. The dashboard then compounds it by hardcoding a `$` prefix (customer-general-section.tsx:148), so even a correct multi-currency customer would be mislabeled as USD.

Here's the plan:

**1. Backend — `packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/helpers.ts`**
- Fetch `orders.currency_code` alongside `orders.total`.
- Change `lifetime_value` from a single `number` to an array grouped by currency: `{ currency_code: string; amount: number }[]`. Don't collapse currencies together — that's the actual bug, not just a missing check.
- `order_count` logic is unaffected (currency-agnostic).

**2. Type — `packages/core/types/src/http/customer/admin/entities.ts`**
- Update `lifetime_value?: number` → `lifetime_value?: { currency_code: string; amount: number }[]`.

**3. Dashboard — `.../customer-general-section/customer-general-section.tsx`**
- Replace the hardcoded `` `$${...toFixed(2)}` `` with a loop over the `lifetime_value` array, formatting each entry via the existing `getStylizedAmount(amount, currency_code)` helper (`packages/admin/dashboard/src/lib/money-amount-helpers.ts:43`) — this is the same helper already used for order totals elsewhere, so it keeps formatting consistent and correctly currency-aware. Render "-" (or a $0 default) when the array is empty.

**4. Tests — `integration-tests/http/__tests__/customer/admin/customer.spec.ts`**
- Update the existing "order_count and lifetime_value" test: since it's now an array, assert `[{ currency_code: "usd", amount: 10000 }]` instead of a bare `10000`.
- Update the "no orders" test: `lifetime_value` should equal `[]` instead of `0`.
- Add a new test: create orders in two currencies (e.g. usd and eur) for the same customer, assert `order_count` sums across both, and `lifetime_value` contains separate correctly-summed entries per currency (not merged).

**5. Changeset**
- Update `.changeset/sour-pants-smile.md` to describe the shape as per-currency lifetime value, since this is a response-shape change reviewers/consumers should know about.

Done. Summary of the fix for the PR comment:

- **`packages/medusa/src/api/admin/customers/helpers.ts`** — `getCustomerOrderStats` now fetches `orders.currency_code` and groups totals by currency instead of blindly summing every order's `total` together.
- **`packages/core/types/src/http/customer/admin/entities.ts`** — `lifetime_value` type changed from `number` to `{ currency_code: string; amount: number }[]`.
- **`customer-general-section.tsx`** — dropped the hardcoded `$` prefix; now renders one line per currency using the existing `getStylizedAmount` helper (same one used for order totals elsewhere), with a `-` fallback when there are no orders.
- **`customer.spec.ts`** — updated the two existing assertions to the new array shape, and added a new test creating orders in `usd` and `eur` for one customer, verifying `order_count` sums across currencies while `lifetime_value` keeps them as separate, correctly-summed entries.
- **Changeset** — updated wording to reflect the per-currency shape.

Verified: `@medusajs/medusa` builds clean, `@medusajs/dashboard` typechecks clean, and all 16 tests in `customer.spec.ts` pass (including the new multi-currency case).

Nothing else touches this response shape elsewhere in the codebase, so this should be safe to push as a follow-up commit addressing the review comment.
